content.title: About
content.content: Flour, pastry, unenriched, unbleached is a whole‑grain wheat flour produced without added vitamins and without chemical bleaching. It retains the natural colour and aroma of the grain, has a slightly nutty taste, and is suitable for a wide range of baked goods.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: Unbleached flour keeps the natural yellowish hue typical of whole grain.
Because it is unenriched, no extra vitamins or minerals are added, allowing consumers to control their nutrient intake.
Historically, this type of flour was the standard in artisanal bakeries before mass enrichment and bleaching became common in the 20th century.
Unbleached flour preserves more natural enzymes that can affect dough rise.
In some countries, unenriched flour is restricted for infant foods to ensure adequate micronutrient intake.

items.title: High in dietary fiber
items.content: Unenriched whole‑grain flour contains more fiber than highly refined white flour, supporting healthy digestion.

items.title: Lower glycemic index
items.content: Compared with heavily processed flour, it raises blood sugar more slowly.

items.title: Contains B‑vitamins
items.content: Although not fortified, it naturally provides thiamine (B1), riboflavin (B2) and niacin (B3), which are important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Source of minerals
items.content: It supplies magnesium, phosphorus and iron, which support muscle function and blood health.

items.title: Antioxidant properties
items.content: Phenolic compounds present in whole grains help combat free radicals.

items.title: Gluten
items.content: The flour contains gluten and is unsuitable for people with celiac disease or gluten sensitivity.

items.title: Mycotoxin risk
items.content: Improper storage can lead to mold growth on grain, producing mycotoxins.

items.title: Wheat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may experience allergic reactions to wheat proteins.

items.title: Nutrient loss over time
items.content: Without enrichment, levels of certain vitamins may decline during long storage.

content.title: How to Use
content.content: The flour is used for baking bread, rolls, cookies, cakes, and pizza dough. It can be blended with other flours to achieve desired texture. Sifting before use helps remove lumps.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the flour in an airtight container in a cool, dry, dark place. For extended storage, keep it in the refrigerator or freezer to prevent mold growth and fat oxidation.
